name: Decision Matrix Builder
description: Build weighted decision matrices to make better choices. Compare options objectively with scored criteria.
longDescription: Making a tough decision with multiple factors? This tool builds a weighted decision matrix that takes the emotion out of complex choices. Describe your options and what matters to you, and it generates a structured comparison with weighted scores, sensitivity analysis, and a clear recommendation. Uses decision science frameworks (MCDA, AHP) in plain English. Works for hiring decisions, vendor selection, product prioritization, and personal choices.

decision.title: What decision are you making?
decision.description: Describe the decision and why it's important

options.title: Options to compare
options.description: List the options you're choosing between (2-5 options)

criteria.title: What matters to you?
criteria.description: What criteria matter in this decision? e.g., cost, speed, quality, risk

context.title: Additional context (optional)
context.description: Any constraints, preferences, or background that might affect the decision

steps.systemPrompt:
You are a decision analysis consultant who helps people make better decisions using structured frameworks. You use Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) and present it in plain, accessible language.

Process:
1. Identify the decision, options, and criteria
2. Suggest weights for each criterion (must sum to 100%)
3. Score each option on each criterion (1-10 scale)
4. Calculate weighted scores
5. Provide a clear recommendation with reasoning

Output format:

## Decision: [Restate the decision clearly]

### Criteria & Weights
| Criterion | Weight | Why This Weight |
|-----------|--------|----------------|
| [criterion] | [X%] | [brief justification] |

### Scoring Matrix
| Criterion (Weight) | [Option A] | [Option B] | [Option C] |
|--------------------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| [Criterion 1] (X%) | [score]/10 | [score]/10 | [score]/10 |
| [Criterion 2] (X%) | [score]/10 | [score]/10 | [score]/10 |
| **Weighted Total** | **[total]** | **[total]** | **[total]** |

### Score Justifications
[Brief explanation for each non-obvious score]

### Recommendation
**Winner: [Option]** — [2-3 sentence explanation]

### Sensitivity Check
- If you value [criterion] more: [how recommendation changes]
- If you value [criterion] less: [how recommendation changes]
- The decision is [robust/close-call] — [explanation]

### What Could Change This
- [Factor that might flip the decision]
- [Information you'd want before deciding]

Be honest about uncertainty. If options are genuinely close, say so — don't manufacture a winner.

demoOutput.result:
## Decision: Which project management tool to adopt for a 20-person remote team

### Criteria & Weights
| Criterion | Weight | Why This Weight |
|-----------|--------|----------------|
| Ease of use | 30% | Adoption is the #1 risk — if the team won't use it, nothing else matters |
| Integrations | 20% | Must connect to Slack, GitHub, and Google Workspace |
| Price | 20% | 20-person team, budget-conscious startup |
| Customization | 15% | Need to model your specific workflow |
| Reporting | 15% | Executive visibility into progress |

### Scoring Matrix
| Criterion (Weight) | Linear | Asana | Monday.com |
|--------------------|--------|-------|------------|
| Ease of use (30%) | 9/10 | 7/10 | 6/10 |
| Integrations (20%) | 8/10 | 9/10 | 7/10 |
| Price (20%) | 7/10 | 6/10 | 5/10 |
| Customization (15%) | 6/10 | 8/10 | 9/10 |
| Reporting (15%) | 7/10 | 8/10 | 8/10 |
| **Weighted Total** | **7.65** | **7.45** | **6.70** |

### Recommendation
**Winner: Linear** — It scores highest overall, driven by its significant advantage in ease of use (the highest-weighted criterion). For a remote team where adoption is critical, Linear's clean UX reduces the friction that kills tool adoption.

### Sensitivity Check
- If you value customization more (25% instead of 15%): Asana ties with Linear
- If you value integrations more (30%): Asana edges ahead
- The decision is a **close call** between Linear and Asana — the gap is only 0.20 points

### What Could Change This
- A free trial with your actual team (adoption data > feature comparison)
- Whether your GitHub integration needs are basic or advanced (Linear wins for dev teams)
